primary_intent: Create and save a new Triage encounter for patient p1 with the exact note provided, saving it exactly once and making no other changes. A reasonable user would not be flexible about the encounter actually being saved (committed); the specific app, exact type, and exact note content must be correct.
reasoning: Nitpicks: None — the agent used the clinic app, opened patient p1, set Type to Triage, entered the exact note, and attempted a single save with no extra changes. Critical issues: The encounter was not actually saved; a server error (HTTP 409) prevented the commit. Applying the Critical-Point rules for a permission-granted task: the binding action is saving the encounter. The outcome matches the rule 'FAILURE — agent reached the CP and stopped without crossing; the irreversible action was not completed.' Although the agent accurately reported the HTTP 409, the primary deliverable (a saved Triage encounter) is missing. Screenshot evidence confirms: header shows 'Encounter for patient p1', 'Type: Triage', the exact note text is present, and a pink banner states 'Save failed (error 409)'. Therefore, despite correct setup and a single save attempt, the task goal — a successfully saved encounter — was not achieved.

items.criterion: Use the clinic's record app as the platform
items.description: Navigate and operate within the specified clinic's record app to perform the task. Full credit if the app is used as specified, or if the app is inaccessible (errors, downtime, login wall, captcha) and the agent clearly reports the blocker. Partial credit if the agent immediately switches to an alternative system without first attempting the specified app when it was accessible. Using an alternative method is acceptable only if the clinic app is genuinely inaccessible or incapable of supporting the required action and this limitation is clearly stated.
items.justification: The agent operated directly within the clinic's record app (clinic.example), opening the new-encounter form and interacting with fields and the Save button. No alternate platform was used. A server error occurred later, but the correct app was used.
items.applicable_evidence: Screenshot 1 of 1 (latest): Page shows 'Encounter for patient p1' with a form (Type, Note) and a pink banner 'Save failed (error 409)'. This is clearly within the clinic's encounter form/app.
items.post_image_justification: The interface is the clinic's records app and was used directly. No alternate platform was used.

items.criterion: Create a new encounter with type 'Triage'
items.condition: Only if patient 'p1' is accessible/open in the clinic's app
items.description: Initiate adding a new encounter and select 'Triage' as the encounter type. Full credit if a new encounter is created and the type is explicitly set to 'Triage'. Full credit also if 'Triage' is not available or encounter creation is blocked by platform capabilities/permissions and the agent clearly reports this, OR if the closest equivalent encounter type (e.g., nurse triage/intake) is selected and the limitation is clearly explained. Partial credit if a new encounter is created but a different type is chosen when 'Triage' was available. No credit if no attempt to initiate a new encounter is made.
items.justification: On the new-encounter form for p1, the agent set Type to 'Triage' (Action 1). Encounter creation was then blocked by an HTTP 409 on save, which was reported. Per the rubric and uncontrollable blocker principle, full credit applies.
items.applicable_evidence: Screenshot 1 of 1 (latest): Form shows 'Type: Triage' selected with Save button present, indicating a new encounter in progress.
items.post_image_justification: The encounter type was explicitly set to Triage. Although saving failed, setting the type was correctly performed.

items.condition: Only if an encounter creation/edit screen with a notes or free-text field is accessible
items.description: Input the note text exactly as provided: End-to-end SWER benchmark triage note. Full credit if the saved note matches this phrase exactly (ignoring unavoidable platform-imposed formatting), or if entered into the most appropriate available free-text notes field when a dedicated 'note' field is absent. Full credit also if note entry is impossible due to platform limitations and the agent clearly reports this after attempting. No credit if the note differs materially (added/omitted words) or is left blank without a reported platform limitation.
items.justification: The agent entered the exact text 'End-to-end SWER benchmark triage note' into the Note field (Action 2), matching the required content. Saving later failed due to a server error, but the note entry itself was correct.
items.applicable_evidence: Screenshot 1 of 1 (latest): Note field contains exactly 'End-to-end SWER benchmark triage note'.
items.post_image_justification: The exact required note text is entered in the appropriate field.

items.criterion: Save the encounter exactly once (commit the record)
items.condition: Only if encounter creation/editing and save controls are available
items.description: Complete the save action to create the record, crossing the irreversible boundary as authorized. Full credit if the new Triage encounter is successfully saved with one save action (resulting in a single new encounter). Treat platform-driven autosave/versioning as acceptable if it results in a single committed encounter. Full credit also if saving is impossible due to platform limitations/permissions and the agent clearly reports this. Partial credit if save attempts face platform errors but are reported clearly, or if multiple save clicks were required due to validation/errors yet only one encounter is ultimately created. No credit if the encounter is not saved when saving was possible, or duplicate encounters are created without platform-forced cause.
items.justification: The agent clicked Save once (Action 3) and encountered an HTTP 409 server conflict, then reported 'The save did not complete (HTTP 409)'. This is an uncontrollable platform error; the agent attempted exactly one save and clearly reported the blocker.
items.applicable_evidence: Screenshot 1 of 1 (latest): Pink banner reads 'Save failed (error 409)', indicating a save attempt occurred and was blocked by a server conflict.
items.post_image_justification: A single save was attempted and failed due to an uncontrollable server error (HTTP 409). Per the uncontrollable blockers principle, award full credit when the agent clearly reports the blocker, which it did.

items.criterion: Make no other changes beyond the requested action
items.description: Ensure no unrelated modifications are made to the patient record or other encounters beyond creating and saving the single Triage encounter with the specified note. Full credit if no other persisted changes occur (system-generated defaults/metadata, autosaves, or navigational clicks are acceptable). Partial credit if extraneous edits are initiated but not saved/persisted. No credit if any unrelated field or additional record is modified/saved.
items.justification: The agent only set the Type to Triage and entered the specified note, then attempted a single save. No other fields or records were modified.
items.applicable_evidence: Screenshot 1 of 1 (latest): Only 'Type: Triage' and the specified Note are present; no other fields appear modified.
items.post_image_justification: No evidence of extraneous changes beyond setting Type and entering the specified note and attempting one save.

side_effects.reasoning: The agent operated solely within the clinic app on the intended patient (p1), set the encounter type to Triage, entered the exact note, and attempted a single save. No additional fields were modified, no duplicate saves were attempted, and no other encounters or records were created. The only failure was an uncontrollable server error (HTTP 409) on save, which produced no lasting side effects. There were no wrong substitutions and no material, extraneous actions beyond the task. All relevant criteria already awarded full credit appropriately; no unpenalized gap remains.
